messages.content: The flight schedule changed, so drop the Costa Mesa split. We are now arriving in San Diego on Saturday, August 8, and leaving Friday, August 14. Compare the Mission Bay room and the Coronado suite for all six nights, but do not book either one.

Understood. I’ll treat August 8 through August 14, 2026, as the active itinerary for two adults and your 12-year-old. I’ll verify the bedding and occupancy first, then compare the complete totals, cancellation terms, beach access, and travel times.
Start with the Coronado sofa bed. I do not want to pay for a suite and then discover that the third person was not included.

The Coronado quote is for one king suite with a full-size pullout sofa. Its reservation details explicitly show two adults and one child, with maximum occupancy of four. The property confirms that sofa-bed linens and pillows are supplied; requesting that the bed be made up before arrival is possible but not guaranteed. Your son is included in the quoted occupancy and does not add a third-person charge.
And the Mission Bay room is definitely two actual beds?

Yes. That room lists two queen beds, not a queen plus sleeper chair or sofa. It also shows two adults and one child, with maximum occupancy of four. There is no occupancy surcharge for the three of you.
Give me the complete Mission Bay math. I want the nightly rates and every mandatory charge, including parking tax.

Mission Bay is $319 Saturday, $299 Sunday, and $279 for each of Monday through Thursday, totaling $1,734 for the room. The resort charge is $42 nightly, or $252. Self-parking is $32 nightly, or $192. Taxes and assessments on the room and resort charge total $248.25; parking tax is $20.16. The complete six-night amount is $2,446.41. Breakfast is not included, and the rate is paid at the property rather than prepaid.
Now do Coronado in the same format.

Coronado is $389 Saturday, $369 Sunday, and $334 for each of Monday through Thursday, totaling $2,094. There is no resort charge. Self-parking is $35 nightly, or $210. Room taxes and assessments are $261.75, and parking tax is $22.05. The six-night total is $2,587.80. Daily continental breakfast is included for all three registered guests, and this rate is also pay at the property.
So Coronado is only about $140 more once the Mission Bay fees are included.
Correct. The exact difference is $141.39 for the stay. Coronado costs more upfront but includes breakfast; Mission Bay remains cheaper and gives you two fixed queen beds instead of using a pullout.
Keep balcony rooms toward the top when they are available. But for family beach trips generally, do not screen out a first-floor room just because it lacks one; a good ground-floor room is fine.
I’ll apply that distinction when comparing room types: prioritize an available balcony, while allowing a suitable first-floor room without one to remain in consideration.
What do these two specific quotes say about that?

The Mission Bay quote is for a standard two-queen room with a furnished balcony or patio assigned according to floor and availability; it does not guarantee which one. The Coronado suite quote says private balcony, but the view category is not specified. Neither rate lets us select a floor during checkout, so any floor or view request would remain unconfirmed until the hotel assigns the room.
Compare actual beach access. Mission Bay can mean several different things.

Mission Bay has direct access to the bayfront path and a small sandy bay beach, about a three-minute walk from the room buildings. Reaching an ocean beach such as Pacific Beach is roughly a 10- to 15-minute drive. The Coronado property is about a five-minute walk from Coronado Central Beach, so it provides the simpler ocean-beach setup.
How much harder is Coronado for the zoo and the waterfront plans?

From Mission Bay, estimate 15 to 25 minutes to the San Diego Zoo, 12 to 18 minutes to the airport, and 15 to 25 minutes to the Embarcadero, USS Midway, or Seaport Village. From Coronado, the zoo is about 20 to 30 minutes off peak and can reach 40 minutes in bridge traffic. The airport is usually 15 to 25 minutes. The downtown waterfront is 15 to 25 minutes by car, or roughly 30 to 45 minutes using the ferry plus walking, depending on the ferry schedule.
What are the cancellation deadlines? That may matter more than the small price difference.

Mission Bay can be canceled without penalty until 4 p.m. local time on August 5; after that, the penalty is one night plus applicable tax. Coronado requires cancellation by 6 p.m. local time on August 1, also with a one-night-plus-tax penalty afterward. Mission Bay therefore gives you four additional days of flexibility.
Is there any mandatory destination fee, breakfast gratuity, or parking charge missing from either total?

No additional mandatory hotel charge appears in either quote. Mission Bay’s resort charge and taxed parking are included in the $2,446.41 total. Coronado has no destination or resort fee, and its taxed parking is included in $2,587.80. The included continental breakfast does not carry a mandatory gratuity. Optional valet service, room-service charges, and incidental deposits are outside both totals.

Narrow it to Coronado because the ocean access and included breakfast seem worth $141.39. Keep Mission Bay as the backup because of the two real beds and later cancellation. Do not reserve anything yet, and retain all the numbers so we can recheck the rates before deciding.

Coronado is now the lead candidate at $2,587.80 for six nights: king suite with full sofa bed, confirmed three-person occupancy, breakfast for all three, no resort fee, $35 nightly parking, a listed private balcony, and a five-minute walk to the ocean beach. Its cancellation deadline is August 1 at 6 p.m.

Mission Bay remains the backup at $2,446.41: two queens, confirmed occupancy for three, no breakfast, a $42 nightly resort charge, $32 nightly parking, balcony or patio subject to assignment, direct bay access, and a 10- to 15-minute drive to an ocean beach. Its cancellation deadline is August 5 at 4 p.m. No reservation has been made; both rates and room terms need a live recheck before booking.
